trends.name: Iran Strait of Hormuz Oil Bottleneck
trends.summary: Ceasefire with Iran is failing to normalize oil transit through Strait of Hormuz, with flows capped at ~15 vessels/day vs. normal 135/day. Only ~55% chance of normalization before July 1. Trump administration pressuring Iran while JPMorgan warns of binary worst-case scenario (resumption of military action triggers WTI spike and equity selloff), creating investor paralysis.

trends.name: Insider Buying Signals Strength
trends.summary: 26.4% of US public companies saw net insider purchases in March (highest in 5 months), up from 20.9% in February. This 2nd consecutive monthly increase and above 10-year average suggests corporate insiders are not bearish despite Iran war risks, signaling confidence in earnings and valuations.

trends.name: Record M&A Activity Surge
trends.summary: Global M&A jumped +18% YoY in Q1 2026 to $1.25 trillion, the largest Q1 on record. Major deals include Unilever's $44.8B food business sale to McCormick and Sysco's $29.1B acquisition, indicating strong capital deployment and mega-deal appetite despite macro uncertainty.

trends.name: AI Competition Intensifies
trends.summary: OpenAI publicly attacked Anthropic as rival gains momentum; Anthropic rolled out Mythos model with security implications. Alibaba leading $290M investment for new AI model architecture amid LLM limitations. Intense competitive dynamics and capital race reshaping AI sector valuations.

trends.name: China Reflation and Factory Prices
trends.summary: China factory prices returned to growth after 3 years, beating expectations amid surging oil prices. Chinese state oil firms tapping reserves as war drags on. Signals China's economic stabilization could support global commodity and energy markets.

trends.name: Fed Chair Confirmation Delayed
trends.summary: Kevin Warsh's Fed chair confirmation hearing hit significant snags and was delayed, creating uncertainty around Fed policy direction and monetary stance. Timing of confirmation impacts market expectations for rate trajectory and inflation management.

trends.name: Tech Stock Divergence and Software Lag
trends.summary: Jim Cramer highlighted divergence in tech stocks with software significantly lagging hardware and AI plays. Indicates rotation within tech sector as investors reassess valuations and growth prospects in light of AI disruption and competitive pressures.

trends.name: Energy Inflation and Food Costs
trends.summary: Iran war risks and oil supply concerns threaten to escalate grocery bills and food inflation through higher energy and transportation costs. UK PM Starmer cited geopolitical tensions affecting energy costs. Investors positioning through commodity and food inflation hedges.

trends.name: Corporate Profit Health Strong
trends.summary: Corporate profits remain very healthy, supporting equity valuations. Earnings season ahead with Netflix and big banks facing reality checks. Strong profitability backdrop suggests valuations justified despite macro risks.

trends.name: EU-US Tech Relations Deteriorate
trends.summary: Trump administration expressing anger over EU Big Tech fines exceeding $7 billion in 2 years. Rising geopolitical tensions between US and EU on regulatory enforcement could impact tech stocks and cross-border trade relationships.

trends.name: Uniqlo Record Highs on Profit Boost
trends.summary: Fast Retailing (Uniqlo parent) shares soared to record highs after lifting profit forecast in Q2 2026. Strong performance in Asian retail provides bright spot amid economic uncertainty and geopolitical risks.

trends.name: Cease-Fire Rally Sustainability Questioned
trends.summary: Analysts warn cease-fire rally may have pushed stocks too high too quickly and could reverse if tensions resume. Trump military buildup in region (70+ transport planes in 24 hours) suggests possible ground offensive preparation, making rally fragile and timing-dependent on geopolitical stability.
